acceptance_claims.claim: A released parent acceptance contract uniquely identifies each bounded responsibility and conserves claim ownership, obligations and provider bindings without relying on hand-written status.
An exact material candidate and accepted facts are reconciled with actual execution coverage of required verification methods; omitted or undiscovered verification cannot qualify a claim.
Parent and child issue read models and the related pull-request read view share one verifiable responsibility basis while retaining separate delivery and review lifecycles.
A successor receives a source-bound, frozen reconstruction basis and is required to detect stale material and obligations before any unsafe continuation; custody does not emerge from the projection.

Agent/reviewer quality observations link to an exact responsibility and independently assessed corpus; unavailable adjudication stays unknown, and advisory health cannot govern progress or acceptance.

An integrated real-history replay demonstrates consistent reconstruction of plan, current material, verification, provider views, successor context and agent advice under misleading and clean controls.

responsibilities.outcome: One released acceptance contract uniquely identifies its responsible owner, exact obligations, and current material binding without relying on titles or prose.
responsibilities.independence_basis: This contract can be accepted or rejected from parent-claim allocation, frozen digest and provider identity before any qualification or status view exists.

semantic_units.outcome: A programme's acceptance obligations are traceable to one immutable responsibility identity and release.
A changed claim, unit or bound provider reference cannot silently retain the preceding contract's authority.
A missing or stale canonical plan is surfaced as an explicit unresolved source rather than a fabricated percentage.
